text: Bar's shut until the Cup's over -- I'm playing in it, which I regret already. Back room stays open. It always stays open.
You're the one Wren's teaching. Go and get taught, then come back and I'll show you the part nobody bothers with.
Right. You know how the stones work, so here is the thing that decides games, which nobody ever teaches because it is arithmetic and arithmetic is boring.
The end. Passing, counting, what a captured stone is actually worth. I have won three hundred games I had no business winning and every one of them was in the last twenty moves.
You've had the lesson. Now the other half of it, which is somebody making you do it under pressure.
One game. That's the rule and it has always been the rule -- one a day, and I mean it, because a man who plays four games a day is not thinking about any of them.

exit.intro: One game. Back room rules -- it goes on the hooks.

text: Mm. You counted that better than I did, and I have been counting since before you were born.
That's the whole compliment. Don't wait for another one.
Good game. You were ahead in the middle and you gave it back a point at a time in the last thirty moves.
That's not a criticism, that's everybody. It's just that I stopped doing it, and that is the only reason I am eight kyu.
Suit yourself. Back room's always open.
Three rated games won. That's three people who sat down expecting to beat you and went home not having. I keep the cards, I notice.
There's a board under the coats at the back table. Thirteen lines. Nine by nine you can hold in your head -- thirteen you have to count, and counting is the only thing I actually know.
Same rule as ever. One game. It goes on the hooks like the rest.

exit.intro: Thirteen lines. Count twice and play once.

text: Back table's still up. Thirteen. One a day and I do mean it.

exit.intro: Thirteen again. The corners are still the cheap part.

text: Hold on. You've got a rank now, so you've got a card.
Back wall. Brass hooks, seven of them, and yours goes on the bottom one because that is where everybody's goes.
It is not the league. The league is a piece of paper in Essenveld with a woman standing next to it. This is a row of hooks, and it says who has beaten who in this room.

choices.text: How do I move up it?

text: Beat somebody hanging above you and you take their hook. They shuffle down. That's it, that's the whole thing.
Losing costs you nothing, before you ask. A ladder where you can go backwards is a ladder nobody ever challenges up.
And every game counts. The park counts. Whatever happens under the arches counts, and I don't want to know the details.
I moved your card up this morning. Somebody's is underneath it now who was above it last week.
They'll have noticed. That's the point of hooks rather than a spreadsheet -- you can see it from the door.
Top hook.
Sixty years that wall's been there and I have seen four people on that hook. Two of them were Joos, twice, with a gap in between I am not going to explain.
Doesn't mean you're the strongest in the room. Means you beat everyone above you on the way up, which is a different sentence and a better one.
